gold_answer_draft.issue: Trace the devolution of title to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 3, Alwis Road, Nugegoda (Lot A in Plan No. 135) from Kanthi Perera, in whom title was allotted by the final decree of 5 September 2005 in Partition Case No. 371/P, down to the persons who own it today, identifying at each intestate death which heirs took and on what statutory footing.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Intestate succession to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (s.21(1)), which applies to the estates of persons dying after its proclamation (s.20) and to persons not governed by Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Tesawalamai (s.2). A surviving spouse takes one-half (s.22); subject to that, inheritance runs in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals (s.23). Children are preferent and take equally per capita, issue of a deceased child taking by representation (s.24). Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, that parent takes half and the other half goes to full-blood brothers and sisters together with half-blood brothers and sisters related through the deceased parent (s.25). Where both parents are dead the collateral share goes to brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood (s.26). Section 27 fixes how full and half blood divide: the fund is halved, the full siblings sharing one half with the father's-side half siblings and the other half with the mother's-side half siblings, but where half siblings of one side only qualify the full siblings take one-half in the first place and divide the remainder with them. Those equally near in degree take per capita (s.30). An administrator's power extends to the deceased's immovable property (Civil Procedure Code s.542), and deeds affecting immovable property require notarial execution (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2). The Ordinance is silent on the effect of a reserved life interest and on its extinction at the death of the life holder, and by s.36 those questions fall to Roman-Dutch law, which is outside the material available here.
gold_answer_draft.application: Kanthi Perera became sole owner under the final decree of 5 September 2005. By Deed of Gift No. 1663 of 20 January 2006 she gifted the property absolutely and irrevocably to Suneth, reserving life interests to herself and to Kamal, so Suneth held the ownership from that date burdened by the two life interests. On Kanthi's death on 18 August 2006 her life interest determined and no ownership interest in this land passed from her, so her children Salinga, Suneth, Lalani and Akash took nothing from her here. Suneth died on 1 July 2008 intestate, unmarried and without issue, owning the property subject to Kamal's surviving life interest. Descendants failing and his mother having predeceased him, s.25 gives his father Kamal one-half and gives the other half to the full-blood siblings Lalani and Akash together with Salinga, the half-sister related through the deceased parent Kanthi; Ravi, related only through the surviving parent Kamal, is excluded by the words of s.25. Applying the one-side proviso in s.27 to that sibling half, Lalani and Akash take one-half of it in the first place, one-eighth each of the whole, and divide the remaining quarter with Salinga per capita under s.30, one-twelfth each. Suneth's estate having been administered in Testamentary Case No. 1231/2008/T, Administrator's Conveyance No. 2635 of 22 December 2008, executed by Kamal under the power described in Civil Procedure Code s.542 and notarially attested as Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 requires, formalised that vesting. Kamal then held twelve twenty-fourths, Lalani five twenty-fourths, Akash five twenty-fourths and Salinga two twenty-fourths. Kamal died on 2 January 2012 intestate; his life interest determined and his one-half passed under s.24 to his surviving children Ravi, Lalani and Akash equally per capita, Suneth having predeceased him leaving no issue to represent him, so each took one-sixth. The holdings then stood at Lalani nine twenty-fourths, Akash nine twenty-fourths, Ravi four twenty-fourths and Salinga two twenty-fourths. Akash died on 4 June 2013 intestate and issueless leaving his wife Seena. Under s.22 Seena took one-half of his nine twenty-fourths. Both his parents being dead, the remaining half fell to his collaterals under s.26, divided by the two-part rule in s.27: one half of it shared by his full sister Lalani with his father's-side half-brother Ravi, and the other half shared by Lalani with his mother's-side half-brother Salinga.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs from Kanthi Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 1663, to Suneth Perera subject to two life interests; from Suneth on his intestacy in 2008 to Kamal as to one-half and to Lalani, Akash and Salinga as to the other half, confirmed by Administrator's Conveyance No. 2635; from Kamal on his intestacy in 2012 to Ravi, Lalani and Akash; and from Akash on his intestacy in 2013 to his widow Seena as to one-half and to Lalani, Ravi and Salinga as to the other. The present owners are therefore Lalani, Ravi, Salinga and Seena, both life interests having determined. This is a proposed statutory map only: the steps that depend on the nature and extinction of the reserved life interests, and the effect of the partition final decree, rest on authority outside the statutes available here.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Quantify the undivided shares in the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 3, Alwis Road, Nugegoda presently owned by each surviving heir, after the three intestacies of Suneth in 2008, Kamal in 2012 and Akash in 2013.
gold_answer_draft.rule: The fractions follow from the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance. Section 22 gives a surviving spouse one-half; s.23 orders the remainder among descendants, ascendants and collaterals; s.24 gives children equal per capita shares with representation for the issue of a deceased child; s.25 gives a sole surviving parent one-half and gives the other half to full-blood siblings and to half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent; s.26 sends the collateral share to brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood where both parents are dead; s.27 halves that share between the father's side and the mother's side, with a proviso that where qualifying half siblings are on one side only the full siblings take one-half in the first place and divide the rest with them; and s.30 makes the division within each class per capita.
gold_answer_draft.application: Taking the whole land as one hundred and ninety-two parts, Suneth's death in 2008 gave Kamal ninety-six parts under s.25 and gave the sibling half of ninety-six parts to Lalani, Akash and Salinga under s.25 read with the s.27 proviso, so that Lalani and Akash took forty parts each and Salinga sixteen. Kamal's death in 2012 divided his ninety-six parts equally under s.24 among Ravi, Lalani and Akash, thirty-two parts each, leaving Lalani seventy-two, Akash seventy-two, Ravi thirty-two and Salinga sixteen. Akash's death in 2013 gave Seena one-half of his seventy-two parts, that is thirty-six, under s.22; the other thirty-six fell to his collaterals under s.26 and were halved by s.27, eighteen shared by Lalani with the father's-side half-brother Ravi and eighteen shared by Lalani with the mother's-side half-brother Salinga, so Lalani gained eighteen, Ravi nine and Salinga nine.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: On this reading the present undivided shares are Lalani ninety parts of one hundred and ninety-two, that is fifteen thirty-seconds; Ravi forty-one parts of one hundred and ninety-two; Salinga twenty-five parts of one hundred and ninety-two; and Seena thirty-six parts of one hundred and ninety-two, that is three-sixteenths. The four fractions total the whole. The figures are proposed only, and they depend on the contestable application of the s.27 proviso to the sibling half created by s.25; on the alternative reading that the sibling half is divided equally in thirds, the shares become Lalani five-twelfths, Ravi five twenty-fourths, Salinga five twenty-fourths and Seena one-sixth.

answer_claims.claim_text: A sole surviving parent takes one-half of the intestate's estate and the remaining half goes to the full-blood siblings and to the half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent.
Where qualifying half-blood siblings are on one side only, the full-blood siblings take one-half of the fund first and divide the remainder with them per capita.

Kamal's ninety-six parts were divided equally among Ravi, Lalani and Akash, thirty-two parts each.

A surviving spouse takes one-half; where both parents of the intestate are dead the other half goes to the brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood, divided into a father's-side part and a mother's-side part.
Akash's seventy-two parts were divided as thirty-six to Seena, eighteen to Lalani, nine to Ravi and nine to Salinga.
